sections.html:
Three offices share the work, and all of them sit in the Sevier County Courthouse at 125 Court Avenue in Sevierville. The Assessor values the land and buildings, the County Commission sets the rate, and the Trustee prints the bills and collects the money. Knowing which desk answers which question saves you a lot of walking between floors.

  • Property Assessor: Suite 210 West, 865.453.3242, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The staff appraise, classify and assess taxable property, and they update ownership and tax maps from recorded deeds.
  • Trustee: Room 212W, (865) 453-2767, same hours. Use the west-end doors and it is the first office on your right. A payment drop box stands behind the courthouse, where the 30 minute parking area meets West Bruce Street.
  • Clerk and Master: Suite 108 W, (865) 453-4654. Delinquent accounts land here, and so does the annual tax sale auction.

Sevierville, Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg all sit inside the county. Ask the city hall for your address whether a separate city bill applies.

Sevier County has 101,342 people as of July 2025 and 62,724 housing units, and 70.7% of households own their home. The typical value of an owner-occupied home is $299,000. There were 1,139 building permits in 2025. Cabin rentals have multiplied around Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge, so many sellers here own a nightly rental rather than a primary home. The Assessor runs an online filing for nightly rentals, and the county posts a short-term rental tax estimator beside its primary home and vacant land estimator.

sections.h2: How a Sevier County tax bill is figured
sections.html:
Tennessee starts with the appraised value, applies an assessment ratio set by state law, and multiplies the result by the local rate. Residential and farm land is assessed at one quarter of appraised value, and commercial or industrial land at 40 percent. Rates are stated for each hundred dollars of assessed value. The Trustee's FAQ listed $1.48 for 2024.

Sevier County reappraises on a five-year cycle, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The Assessor has to review roughly 90,000 parcels. A certified rate is then calculated under state law to hold total collections steady, and the Board of Commissioners adopts the final figure. Some owners will see higher bills and some lower, so read the 2026 bill itself.

Between cycles, values stay put unless the property physically changes. A sale or other change in ownership does not move the assessment by itself.

The 2026 bills were mailed in early October and can be paid from October 1 onward without penalty, through the end of February 2027. After that, interest of 1.5 percent accrues every month on the unpaid base amount. Mailed checks need a postmark dated no later than the last day, because the Trustee refuses office meter dates. Card and e-check payments count on the day of the transaction. Partial payments are accepted, and only the leftover balance collects interest.

Sevier County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for ownership, assessments and tax maps
March 1Business personal property schedules and greenbelt applications due
MayAssessment change notices mailed
June 1Board of Equalization opens appeal hearings
First week of OctoberTrustee mails bills; payable from October 1
End of FebruaryLast day to pay without interest

The Trustee does not send copies to mortgage companies, so if your lender escrows taxes, pass the bill along. Each year's tax covers that calendar year.

Call the Assessor first. If the answer falls short, take the dispute to the Board of Equalization, which begins hearing appeals June 1. The Assessor's reappraisal line is (865) 774-3756, staffed weekday mornings and afternoons, and the email is reappraisal@seviercountytn.gov.

Gather evidence before you call: recent sales of similar houses, repair estimates for defects the appraisal missed, and the facts on square footage or condition. Ask the office for the filing deadline in the current cycle, since notice dates shift. Start when the notice arrives in May rather than waiting for the bill.

The Trustee administers two state programs for homeowners, and staff complete the application with you at the counter. Tax Relief covers all or part of the tax on a home, mobile homes included, for people 65 or older, the disabled, disabled former service members, and their widowed spouses. Posted figures for 2025 taxes:

  • Elderly and disabled owners: household income capped at $37,530 including a spouse, with relief figured on market value up to $32,700
  • Disabled veterans and their surviving spouses: no income test, relief figured on market value up to $175,000
  • Tax Freeze, age 65 and up: income may not exceed $47,990 for 2024, and the application is renewed each year

Relief reaches city taxes too. Greenbelt is a separate break for parcels of 15 acres or more in farm or forestry use, requested by March 1. Land that drops out owes a rollback of the taxes saved over the last three years. Ask the Trustee for this year's limits before you plan around these figures.

The tax lien follows the parcel, so any balance must be cleared at or before closing. The Trustee mails each bill to whoever is listed as owner, and new buyers are told to read the closing statement to learn who handles that year's tax. The title company ordinarily settles any open balance at the table, out of your sale proceeds.

If a bill goes unpaid past the deadline, the account turns delinquent and moves to Chancery Court, where costs are added and the parcel can be advertised for the yearly auction. The Clerk and Master publishes the list 20 to 30 days ahead. Bidders register in person half an hour before the sale starts, and payment is cash, money order or check. The former owner has a year to redeem, and the bidder earns 1 percent per month in the meantime.

If you owe back taxes, phone the Trustee at (865) 453-2767 before the list appears. A cash sale skips the listing, showings and buyer financing delays, so it can close quickly enough to clear a delinquent balance before the auction. Ask for a payoff figure close to the closing date, because costs and interest keep adding up.

faqs.q: Who mails the property tax bill in Sevier County?
faqs.a: The Trustee does, normally in the first week of October. The Assessor values the property and the County Commission picks the rate, but only the Trustee at 125 Court Avenue, Room 212W, collects. Call (865) 453-2767 if no bill shows up.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for paying Sevier County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: The final day of February. For the 2026 bill, that is February 2027. Beginning March 1, interest runs at 1.5 percent monthly (18 percent yearly), and a late postmark counts as a late payment.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sevier County property tax in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes, the Trustee accepts partial payments, and interest builds only on whatever remains once the account is delinquent. Owners 65 or older may also qualify for state Tax Relief or Tax Freeze, both handled in person at the Trustee's office.

faqs.q: How often does Sevier County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every five years, with 2026 as the current reappraisal year. Values hold between cycles unless the property physically changes. After reappraisal, a certified rate is calculated so total collections stay steady.

faqs.q: Will an unpaid Sevier County tax bill stop a sale?
faqs.a: It will not stop the sale, but the balance has to come from sale money because the lien stays on the parcel. Ask the Trustee for the exact payoff on your closing date. Accounts sent to Chancery Court pick up costs and can end in a tax sale.
